 This petition having been heard and reserved for orders
 for pronouncement this day, the court passed the following:
 Order

By this petition preferred under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the petitioner has challenged the order dated 12.12.2019 (Annexure P/1) passed by the Collector, District Barwani whereby the application preferred by him for release of his land has been rejected.

02. As per the petitioner, his land bearing survey No.167/1, 194/1 and 194/4 total area 0.709 hectare Village Silawad, Tehsil and District Barwani was acquired by the State Government for respondent No.5, M.P. Road Development Corporation Limited, Barwani.

entities.text: M.P. Road Development Corporation Limited, Barwani
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Award in that regard was passed on 07.10.2011.
Till date, the petitioner has not received compensation amount as determined under the award and is still in possession of the land.

On 26.08.2015, he had submitted an application to the Collector, District Barwani for release of his acquired land submitting that though the same has been acquired but has not been used by the respondents.

On the said application, response was sought from respondent No.5 which was received to the effect that it is not aware of the status of petitioner's land and the entire information is available with the Land Acquisition Officer,
respondent No.3.

On report having been sought for from the Land Acquisition Officer, by his letter dated 28.07.2015 he intimated that the petitioner has till date not taken the amount of compensation for his acquired land and that the Public Works Department is not in necessity of the land.

03. Thereafter, another application was preferred by the petitioner on 10.11.2015 for release of his acquired land on which spot inspection was carried out by the Revenue Inspector and report was submitted by him on 14.03.2016 stating that petitioner is in possession of the land with construction over a part and the remaining part is lying vacant.

By his report dated 11.04.2016, the Sub Divisional Officer (Barwani) stated that only a part of the land of the petitioner has been utilized and land measuring 0.011 hectare (26 ft. x 40 ft. = 1040 sqft.) is remaining of which the petitioner has not received any compensation and that it would be appropriate to release the said land in his favour.
The Collector thereafter sent a proposal to the State Government for denotification of the aforesaid land of the petitioner concurring with the report of the Sub Divisional Officer.
By his proposal dated 06.11.2017, the Additional Commissioner also wrote to the State Government proposing denotifying the aforesaid land of the petitioner.

However, since no action was taken, the petitioner preferred W.P. No.1786/2016 before this Court which was disposed off by order dated 09.03.2018 with a direction to the Collector to take a final decision in the matter.
Thereafter, the Collector by his order dated 30.08.2018 held that since the matter is pending before the State Government, no further orders are required to be passed on his part.

However, by letter dated 10.04.2019, the State Rajesh vs State Of M.P. Throurh Revenue ... on 30 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110513251/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Government remitted the matter back to the Collector stating that it is the Collector himself, who is the competent authority to take decision on the application of the petitioner for denotification of his land.

Thereafter, the impugned order has been passed by the Collector rejecting the application of the petitioner by observing that it would not be in the interest of the State Government to release the land of the petitioner from acquisition.

04. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the impugned order passed by the Collector is illegal in as much as the previous proceedings in the matter have not at all been taken into consideration by him.

Previously, the Collector himself had recommended to the State Government for release of land of the petitioner stating that it is lying unutilized and that there is no objection in case of the same being released in favor of the petitioner.
The Additional Commissioner had also sent a similar proposal to the State Government.

It is only on account of the matter having been remitted back to the Collector that he was required to pass an order on the application of the petitioner which ought to have been allowed by taking into consideration his own previous recommendation and that of the Additional Commissioner and in view of facts and circumstances of the case.
The impugned order hence deserves to be quashed and the application of the petitioner deserves to be allowed.

05. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents has submitted that the petitioner does not have any vested right to seek denotification /release of land which has been once acquired under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

Even otherwise, the impugned order has accorded reasons of public interest in not releasing the land which once belonged to the petitioner and has been subsequently acquired by affording adequate compensation to the petitioner.
The petitioner has himself not been appearing for receiving the amount of compensation awarded to him.
Since the land already stands vested in the State Government the petitioner cannot contend himself to be in its possession.
There is no provision of law under which the application preferred by the petitioner could have been entertained.
It is hence submitted that the petition deserves to be dismissed.
06. I have considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
07. The land of the petitioner of which he is seeking release from acquisition was acquired by the State Government by passing of an award on 07.10.2011.
As per the petitioner, he has not received any compensation in respect of that land.
He contends that he is in possession of the land.

Earlier by order dated 09.03.2018 passed in W.P. No.1786/2016, the Collector, Barwani was directed to take final decision in the matter as to whether the land is required further or not after taking consent from the concerned department for whom the land in question was acquired.
The Executive Engineer, P.W.D. (Bridge Division) was also permitted to appear before the Collector.
08. However, from a perusal of the impugned order passed by the Collector, Barwani, it does not appear that he has complied with the aforesaid order of this Court.
He was enjoined to adjudicate whether the land of the petitioner is required further or not.
However, no finding has been recorded by him in that regard.
He has merely observed that it would not be in the interest of the State Government to release the land from acquisition.

The Collector has only referred to the proceedings Rajesh vs State Of M.P. Throurh Revenue ... on 30 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110513251/
3 of the case but has not taken into consideration the earlier recommendations made by the respondents themselves particularly the Public Works Department to the effect that the land of the petitioner is not required by the department.

entities.text: Rajesh vs State Of M.P. Throurh Revenue
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Earlier by a letter dated 28.07.2015, the Public Works Department (Bridge Division) had itself written to the Collector that the land is not required by the department.

09. It has also been brought on record by various communications that the purpose for which the land of the petitioner was acquired has been fulfilled after which the land of which the petitioner is seeking release is lying unutilized and vacant.

The Sub Divisional Officer (Barwani) by his letter dated 11.04.2016 and the Collector himself by his letter dated 03.05.2016 had, through the Commissioner, Indore Division, Indore, communicated to the State Government that it would be expedient to denotify the land of the petitioner as prayed for by him under Section 48 of the Act,
1894.
A similar recommendation was made on 12.09.2017 by him.
His recommendation was concurred by the Commissioner, Indore Division, Indore by his communication dated 06.11.2017.
The matter was remitted back to the Collector only because the State Government directed that he is the competent authority to take decision in the matter and not the State Government.

10. From a reading of the impugned order, it is absolutely clear that the Collector has not taken into consideration the previous proceedings of the case whereby recommendation was made by himself as well as the Commissioner to the State Government to the effect that the land of the petitioner deserves to be denotified / released from acquisition.
The order passed by this Court also directing him to decide as to whether the land is required further or not has not been complied with by him.

Merely by observing that it would not be in the interest of the State Government to release the land,
the application of the petitioner has been rejected with cannot be said to be a judicious determination of the matter and hence cannot be sustained.
11. Consequently, the petition deserves to be and is accordingly allowed.

The impugned order dated 12.12.2019 passed by the Collector, District Barwani is set aside and the matter is remanded back to him to redecide the applications preferred by the petitioner for release of his land from acquisition by taking into consideration the entire proceedings of the case which have taken place since the inception up till date and also by ensuring compliance of order dated 09.03.2018 passed by this Court in W.P. No.1786/2016.
The petitioner is directed to appear before the Collector, District Barwani, along with a certified copy of this order on 10.06.2024 for further proceedings.
12. The petition is accordingly allowed and disposed off.

(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE Shilpa Rajesh vs State Of M.P. Throurh Revenue ... on 30 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110513251/
